name: Architectural Lighting

seo.title: Architectural Lighting | DAVG
seo.description: Fixture position, beam shape, driver behavior, and control all affect how a room feels. We plan those decisions together.

hero.heading: Design the light before you choose the keypad.
hero.deck: Fixture position, beam shape, driver behavior, and control all affect how a room feels. We plan those decisions together.

study: One room, three light layers, three times of day. A wall-elevation study connects the lighting design to the actual keypad.

chapters.title: What should the room illuminate?
paragraphs: A bright ceiling does not guarantee a comfortable room. Light aimed at a work surface serves a different job from light on a painting or a quiet path to the kitchen.
Ambient light sets the room. Task light puts light where work happens; accent light gives materials and objects shape.
We map those layers against furniture, finishes, sightlines, and daily use. Then we group the fixtures into circuits that can be adjusted independently.
chapters.visual: Use the same room photograph for ambient, task and accent states. Annotate actual fixture locations rather than decorative glowing lines.

chapters.title: A dimmer is only one part of the chain.
paragraphs: An LED driver converts power for the light source. The dimmer and driver must work together across the brightness range you expect to use.
A mismatch can produce flicker, audible noise, abrupt shutoff, or a low setting that is still too bright. A compatibility check and a representative installed test reveal more than a dimmable label.
Low-end adjustment is part of commissioning. We test the selected fixture, driver, load and control together before repeating that combination throughout the house.
chapters.visual: Exploded fixture → driver → dimming method → control diagram with a low-end test photograph.

chapters.title: Dimming and changing color are different decisions.
paragraphs: Warm-dim light gets warmer as brightness falls. Tunable-white light allows color temperature to change separately from brightness, within the selected product’s range.

Neither approach fixes poor fixture placement or glare. Matching products also requires checking their color behavior together; equal numbers on two specifications do not guarantee an identical appearance.
Choose the behavior by room. An evening living room and a detailed work area may need different control ranges and scene settings.
chapters.visual: Three labeled sample states, photographed with consistent exposure and white balance. Include actual product range only after selection.

chapters.title: Choose the Lutron system around the design.
paragraphs: Caséta can suit focused connected-lighting projects. RadioRA 3 extends the residential system with its supported controls and integrations; HomeWorks supports a broader custom design with additional control and wiring choices.
Centralized dimming moves selected load-control equipment into panels. Local dimming keeps the control at the room; either approach has wiring, service-access and architectural implications.
The right system follows the load schedule, fixtures, interfaces, shades and construction plan. HomeWorks is not required just because a house is expensive.

chapters.title: The wall should explain the room.
paragraphs: A dimmer directly controls a compatible load. A scene keypad sends instructions to the system, so one button can adjust several lighting layers and supported shades.
Sunnata offers a contemporary control language. HomeWorks designs can also use interfaces such as Palladiom, seeTouch and Alisse where the selected system supports them.

Alisse belongs to HomeWorks QSX and uses a wired QS connection. A RadioRA 3 Sunnata RF keypad uses radio for communication but still requires its specified electrical supply; RF does not mean battery-powered.
chapters.visual: Front, wall-installed and material-close-up images for Sunnata, seeTouch, Palladiom and Alisse. Caption exact system, model, finish and button configuration.

chapters.title: Keep the same room. Change the occasion.
paragraphs: Cooking brings the work surfaces forward. Dinner reduces task light and puts more emphasis on the table and surrounding walls.
An evening scene can lower light and close selected shades. A late-night path can light circulation without waking the whole room.
Scene levels are set in the finished space. Stone, timber, fabrics and wall color all change what a percentage setting looks like.
chapters.visual: Repeat the opening room in Cooking, Dinner and Late Night states. Beside it, show one short keypad label list.

projectPaths.title: Work with the existing circuits
projectPaths.body: Check box wiring, drivers, fixtures and circuit groups before selecting replacements. Keep the plan honest about what can change without opening walls.

projectPaths.title: Use the open walls well
projectPaths.body: Coordinate circuit separation, driver locations, wall elevations and new fixtures before electrical rough-in. Test a fixture-and-driver sample before bulk purchase.

projectPaths.title: Coordinate light with architecture
projectPaths.body: Develop fixture locations, beam intent, load schedule, panel space and keypad elevations with the architect, lighting designer and electrician. Reserve access for future service.

scopeOptions.label: Good — room-led scenes
scopeOptions.scope: Selected rooms, compatible dimming, clear everyday controls and commissioned scene levels.
scopeOptions.dependencies: Existing circuit groups may limit independent layers; fixture replacement is explicitly itemized.

scopeOptions.label: Better — coordinated lighting
scopeOptions.scope: Multiple rooms, a lighting-layer plan, interface schedule and coordinated shade scenes.
scopeOptions.dependencies: Platform choice follows load and interface requirements, not the tier label.

scopeOptions.label: Best — architectural lighting design
scopeOptions.scope: Whole-residence planning, detailed fixture/driver review, architectural keypad coordination and full commissioning.
scopeOptions.dependencies: Panelized loads and tunable light are selected only where the design benefits from them.

faqs.question: Can existing LEDs stay?
faqs.answer: Only after the fixture and driver combination is checked with the proposed control. Some replacements may be needed for the requested dimming behavior.

faqs.question: Is a keypad just a more expensive switch?
faqs.answer: A switch operates a circuit. A scene keypad can instruct several loads and systems, which changes both the wiring plan and the way the room is used.

faqs.question: Does HomeWorks replace the lighting designer?
faqs.answer: No. Fixture placement, optics and light quality still need design; the control system manages the agreed loads and scenes.

faqs.question: What drives cost?
faqs.answer: Fixture and driver choices, circuit count, wiring access, panel work, interfaces, tunable lighting and commissioning depth.

inquiry.body: Tell us which rooms matter, what already exists, and when construction starts. Share plans or photographs if you have them.

openingQA.question: Why design the light and its controls together?
answer: Fixture positions and beam shapes determine where light goes. Drivers and compatible controls determine how that light dims and changes.
Planning both lets you create distinct task, ambient and accent layers, then adjust them together for the way the room is used.
